narrative_passages.title: Hud warns 'Ad
narrative_passages.treatment_reason: Hud and ‘Ad are never shown; the punishing wind is read only. Their story is played in Surah Hud’s world.

summary_for_children: Al-Ahqaf means The Wind-Curved Sandhills. It tells of Hud warning 'Ad in the dunes, and teaches kindness to parents. It mentions jinn who listened to the Quran.
environment_concept: Wind-curved dunes (46:21), a cloud approaching the valleys (46:24) and a quiet night valley with standing stones (46:29; nothing unseen is shown).
architecture_and_scenery: Curved sand dunes, empty dwellings, an approaching dark cloud, and a quiet night valley.

palette.lighting: Hot dune light, then storm darkness

areas.name: Listening Valley
areas.description: A quiet night valley; nothing unseen is shown.

activities.name: Kindness to parents
activities.description: Carry water jars home for your parents.

activities.name: Listen quietly

narration_plan: Narration keeps Hud and the jinn unseen.

status.playable_environment: first version built: a composed world (cloud, dunes, stones) with 1 hands-on activity in the scene
status.testing: not tested yet: written and type-checked, not yet checked on screen

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: Long curving sand dunes with a path winding between them to a palm-shaded well

primary_mechanic.text: Set up four palm-frond windbreaks at seven posts beside a path through the dunes, then wait out a windy spell at the well; sand piles up on every stretch with no windbreak upwind, and a buried stretch restarts the spell. The wind of 46:24-25 is read only, never played.

secondary_activities: the brother of ‘Ad among the dunes (46:21-23, read)
unique_world.narrative_structure: The warning among the dunes, the windy spell, the reading of the cloud, then parents and listening
environment_behaviour: sand mounds grow on unprotected stretches of path
the windsock flaps harder in the spell
unique_world.learning_objective: Know where the surah’s name comes from (46:21), and be kind to parents (46:15)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Wind-Curved Dunes
story_library.children_narration: The people of 'Ad lived in a land associated with sand dunes. Prophet Hud warned them, but they rejected his message. The surah also reminds us to care for our parents and describes a group of jinn who listened to the Quran and believed.

world_idea.title: The Singing Sand Dunes
world_idea.description: Explore a wind-shaped desert landscape, investigate the story of 'Ad, and learn about caring for parents through a separate symbolic activity.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The jinn (46:29-32) are not shown, and nothing stands in for them.
